rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 10 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6728, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS GOVERNMENT ASSISTANCE TO STUDENTS AND TEACHERS IN PRIVATE EDUCATION (GASTPE)
rows.abstract: This bill intends to provide a mechanism whereby different sector of our educational system  can equally exercise their rights to express their positions in any proposed increase in the rate of tuition and/or other school fees. Furtheremore, apart from financial statements, the school administration is required to submit expansion and wage increase plans for faculty and non-faculty members. among others. With these, it is hoped that the informed participation of all the affected sectors can besolicited and considered before a major decision such as a tuition fees increase can be made.

rows.abstract: "National Railways Act of 2002". There is hereby created a National Railway Authority (NRA) which shall be primarily responsible for the preparation of a Master Development Plan for a national mass transportation and railway system, including its component regional, provincial, and metropolitan railway systems; the construction, development, operation, maintenance of railway systems, and the financing thereof through borrowings from multi-lateral agencies, BOT or other forms of private financing schemes. The preparation and implementation of the Master Development Plan shall be undertaken with the active and meaningful participation of the private sector, including non-governmenta l and people's organizations, and affected local communitiees.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Cancer patients fr the rural areas find it difficult to avail of treatment facilities, as they are concentrated in Metro Manila. Hence, for the purpose of meeting the health care needs of the people of the entire country, a cancer centershould be established in all regional medical centers of the Philippines. The center must be geographically central to all provinces and easily accessible to patients.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE BOARD FOR PROFESSIONAL TEACHERS TO ISSUE TEMPORARY OR SPECIAL PERMIT TO HOLDERS OF MASTER'S DEGREE IN EDUCATIONAL MANAGEMENT OR INSTRUCTIONAL LEADERSHIP, OR THEIR EQUIVALENT, TO ENGAGE IN TEACHING OR ACT AS PROFESSIONAL TEACHERS FOR A PERIOD OF TWO YEARS
rows.abstract: Rationale: Section 26 of RA 7836, the Philippine Teachers Professional Act of 1992, requires the registration of all teachers as professional teachers. With the expiration of the two-year period within which to register with examination and the five-year special or temporary permit, all teachers must now take and pass the licensure examination before they are allowed to engage in teaching or act as professional teachers. As a consequence, thousand of highly qualified holders of master's degreeare prevented from immediately applying their newly acquired skills, specialized trainings and modern concepts of teaching, to the detriment of education in the country.> In view of the foregoing considerations, approval of this bill is earnestly souught.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05411

rows.abstract: "Magna Carta of Agricultural Officers and Employees of 2002". Rationale: In a nation where more than half of the population relies on agriculture for livelihood and sustenance, the emancipation of our agricultural workers, which are the backbone ofthe country and the sustained grwoth of the countryside are both material and moral imperatives. This means designing and implementing policies that ensure social equity in order that delivery of basic services to the farmers and other sectors may beaffected alongside with economic opportunity and growth in the countryside. The agricultural officer is especially expected to perform the devolved functions in attaining its goal of teaching/assist ing the farmers of modern farm technology to uplifft their living conditions.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Tree planting is just one of the several steps to combat the perennial problem of forest denudation and the consequent flooding of low-lying areas during the wet season of the year. > To protect human lives and prevent economic losses engendered by natural disasters, thereis an urgent need to preserve our forest especially those which are landslide prone areas. The Amendment reads as follows: (1) x x x > "(a) Through force, threat, or intimidation; "(b) When the offended party is deprived of reason or otherwise unconscious; "(c) By means of fraudulent machinations or grace abuse of authority; and "(d) When the offended party is under twelve (12) years of age or is demented, even though none of circumstances mentioned above be present.> "(2) By any person who, under any of the circumstances mentioned in paragraph 1 hereof, shall commit an act of sexual assault by inserting [his] THE penis into another person's mouth or anal orifice, or any instrument, [or] object, OR ANY OTHER PARRT OF THE BODY into the genital or anal orifice of another person."

rows.abstract: This bill gives the Sangguniang Panlalawigan more powers by giving it the power to conduct inquiries in aid of legislation, issue subpoena testificandum and duces tecum and to punish for contempt any person who refuses to obey this process and refuse to be sworn to or answer inquiries whem lawfully required to do so. Anyone who refuses to obey the subpoena or refuses to be sworn to or answer inquiries when lawfully required to do so by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in connected with its legislative function under Section 48 of R.A. 7160 and its quasi-judicial power under Section 62 and 63 and related sections of R.A. 7160 may, after due norice and hearing, be adjudged in contempt and be punished by a fine not exceeding THREE THOUSAND PESOS(P3,000.00) or imprisonment not exceeding ten days, or both at the discretion of the concerned Sangguniang Panlalawigan.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend R.A. No. 7471, otherwise known as "An Act to Promote the Development of Philippine Overseas Shipping" signed on May 5, 1992, by then President Corazon C. rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING THE RIGHT TO FRANCHISEES TO DEVELOP THE RURAL AIRPORT INFRASTRUCTURE NETWORK IN THE PHILIPPINES FOR COMMERCIAL AND OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Our country sorely needs dependable transport systems to make economically convenient and affordable access to and from rural areas. Speedy access between urban and rural areas may be provided only by the construction and maintenance of arural air transport network complemented by the rehabilitation and maintenance of former or existing airports in the remote areas of our archipelago. Government does not have enough to finance the construction of these airports. This bill seeks to provide a way to develop rural airports through the help of the private sector.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2002-03-05

rows.abstract: The amendments intended to strengthen the right to security of tenure of employees deal on the following: (1) When employment is deemed "regular"; (2) Entitlement of a contractrual employee to all rights and privileges; (3) Coverage of specific projects/undert akings for a fixed period; and (4) When an employee is dismissed to just or authorized cause.

rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR REASONABLE COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS FOR THE LOSS OF LIVES, INJURIES AND DAMAGES TO PROPERTY SUFFERED BY NON-COMBATANT INDIVIDUALS IN THE COURSE OF OPERATIONS BY THE MILITARY, POLICE AND/OR OTHER LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES AND FOROTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: A military, police and/or other law enforcement agencies' opertion to suppress rebellion or to pursue and/or apprehend criminal elements, no matter how cautiously conducted, invariably causes damages upon innocent civilians and non-combatants. Unfortunately, there is no existing government mechanism that compensate for these damages that come in the form of physical and/or psychological injuries, death and/or destruction of properties. Hence, the proposed bill seeks to fill in this void in order to prove to the citizenry that the government means no harm to them and that such damages are inevitable consequences of the government's duty to defend itself and protect its pople.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2002-03-05

rows.abstract: Rationale: It is the policy of the State to give highest budgetary priority to education and ensure that teaching will attract and retain its rightful share of the best available talents through adequare remuneration and other means of job satisfaction and fulfillment. This bill provides for the upgrading of teachers' salaries commensurate to their educational attainment and professional preparation that require them to finish a Bachelors degree and to pass the Professional Board Examination for Teachers and considering that teachers are the major componenets of the education process.

rows.author: C017
rows.title_full: AN ACT RENAMING THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AS THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES
rows.title_short: Renaming the Department of Agriculture as the Department of Agriculture and Fisheries
rows.abstract: Rationale: The country's coastal waters is seven (7) times bigger that its land area, yet development efforts have been mostly channeled to crop and livestock production. The perceived neglect of the fisheries sector gives rise to the filing of thisbill. > The bill aims to give emphasis to the importance of the fisheries sector by renaming the Department of Agriculture as the Department of Agriculture and Fisheries. The inclusion of the word "Fisheries" in the name of the Department shall ensure that the fisheries sector will always receive equal attention being given to the agriculture sector.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROMOTION OF BIO-ORGANIC FARMING IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Providing for the Promotion of Bio-Organic Farming in the Philippines
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to implement a comprehensive program that will promote bio-organic cultivation and production methods among farmers and it and encourages research and development in the said field. > The bill provides for the following: (1) The Department of Agriculture (DA) shall take the lead role in the program, supported by all service agencies in their respective areas of concern; (2) Organic input producers shall be provided with financial, technical, marketing and other services and resources of the government; (3) The Bio-Organic Farming Authority/Commi ssion shall be created to be headed by an Executive Director;and (4) The Executive Director is empowered to call upon any government agency for assistance in the performance of his ttasks and to initiate criminal and/or administrative actions under the penal provision of this Act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL FOOD AND BEVERAGE MANUFACTURERS TO PRINT NUTRITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE PRODUCTS' LABEL AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: All food and beverage manufacturers are hereby required to print on the products' label a nutritional information guide which shall enumerate, among others the vitamins, mineral and fat contents of such products: Provided, That if such product is asignificant source of calorie from fat, saturated fat and cholesterol, its manufacture shall likewise be required to print in legible or bold letters "WARNING: SIGNIFICANT SOURCE OF CALORIES FROM FAT, SATURATED FAT AND CHOLESTEROL" on the food labelof such and beverage product. > All importers, consignees, distributors or suppliers of food and beverages which are manufactured abroad and brought into the country, are required prior to the sale or distribution thereof, to print a nutritional infoormation guide as provided for in Section 1 hereof.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2002-03-07

rows.author: D019
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE POSITION OF TOURISM OFFICER WITH THE RANK OF HEAD OF OFFICE OR DEPARTMENT, MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A TOURISM DEPARTMENT/OFFI CE IN ALL LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AND FOR THIS PURPOSE, AMENDING THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTCODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: All government units are hereby mandated to institutionaliz e the position of Tourism Officer as a regular item in their respective units. Such position shall have the rank equivalent to head of office or department. The Tourism Officer shall be under the direct supervision of the Chief Executive of the local government unit. > All local government units are hereby mandated to establish a Tourism Department or Tourism Office in their respective units. Such Department/Offi ce shall be organizedto support the efforts, plans and programs of the Tourism Officer.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2002-03-07

rows.author: D062
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING STIFFER PENALTIES ON ILLEGAL GAMBLING, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED SIXTEEN HUNDRED AND TWO, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: The proliferation of illegal gambling activities throughout the country has been observed to be constantly on the rise and along with it, social ills such as drug addiction, crimes against person and property, and borked family relations. The penalties imposed by the present laws have become inadequate or obsolete to discourage, if not stop, these noxious activities. The imposable penalties on illegal gambling are already impractical, ineffective, and unresponsive to the present norms of conduct and behavior of society because laws on the matter were enacted more than two decades ago. > The penalties for illegal gambling must be INCREASED.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06575
